status: student-selected pilot taxonomy; automatic masks require review
annotation_rules: Unmatched or ambiguous pixels are 255, not background. Background needs positive evidence or manual review.
Label visible pixels, not imagined ground beneath objects. These labels do not grant traversability.

Cast shadows and their lighting boundaries retain the underlying visible surface class. Visible sidewalk under a shadow is class 1, not a person or ignore merely because it is dark. Actual occluding people or objects keep their own classes; visually indeterminate surfaces remain 255.

Ordinary sidewalk cracks, slab seams, expansion joints, and surface stains remain class 1. Do not cut out a joint merely because it is dark or green-tinted. Separately visible objects or protruding vegetation retain their own classes; ambiguous pixels remain 255. This does not reclassify actual holes, raised curb faces, or missing pavement as sidewalk.

For human review, a visibly continuous sidewalk corridor across a driveway stays class 1; the vehicle access surface outside it is class 2. If the boundary cannot be established visually, mark 255. Automatic prompts do not enforce this contextual rule.
Attached vegetation is class 4; a detached branch lying on the path is class 11. Unclear cases are 255.
A curb ramp is class 1; a raised curb face, step, or visible ledge is class 10. Do not infer invisible drop-offs.
Thin edges, holes, distant objects, driveway crossings, and broad surfaces need particular review. Failure to detect them is not evidence of absence.
Original 16-class fine annotations do not yet exist. This direct 12-class run cannot recover merged distinctions without new labeling.
